subject: Accounting
title: The Wirecard Audit Failure
description: A quick, practical guide to The Wirecard Audit Failure.

hook.text: EY audited Wirecard for over a decade and never confirmed that €1.9 billion in cash was real.

buildup.text: The cash was supposedly held in trustee accounts in the Philippines.

discovery.text: EY relied on bank confirmation letters and documents that turned out to be forged.

twist.text: A basic step—directly contacting the banks—was apparently not performed until the very end.

climax.text: The failure led to lawsuits, regulatory investigations, and a crisis of confidence in Big Four audits.

punchline.text: One phone call could have stopped a decade of fraud.

quiz.question: What basic step was missed in the Wirecard audit?
options: Directly verifying cash balances with the banks

details.summary: Wirecard, a German fintech company, collapsed in 2020 when €1.9 billion in reported cash turned out not to exist — despite years of clean audit opinions from EY, raising fundamental questions about audit effectiveness and auditor responsibility.
details.whyItMatters: The Wirecard scandal is the most significant European audit failure of the 21st century and has driven major reform discussions about auditor liability, rotation, and the role of Big Four firms.
takeaways: Wirecard fabricated €1.9 billion in cash balances across Asian bank accounts that never existed
EY issued clean audit opinions for years despite red flags and investigative journalism exposing fraud
The scandal prompted calls for mandatory auditor rotation and increased personal liability for auditors

faq.question: How did Wirecard's fraud go undetected for so long?
faq.answer: Wirecard fabricated bank confirmations and used third-party partnerships in Asia to create fictional revenue. EY reportedly relied on third-party confirmations without directly verifying with banks until 2020. Journalists at the Financial Times flagged problems years before auditors.

faq.question: What reforms resulted from the Wirecard scandal?
faq.answer: Germany overhauled financial regulation, replacing BaFin's audit oversight. The EU accelerated discussions about mandatory auditor rotation, joint audits, and separating audit from consulting. EY faced lawsuits and investigations that continue to reshape accountability.
